nativeBaseline.reference: native editable text input controlling a custom listbox popup

library: combobox/listbox roles and aria-expanded, aria-controls, and aria-activedescendant relationships
DOM focus remains on the editable input while Up/Down Arrow moves the active enabled visible option
popup options are excluded from the sequential Tab order and disabled options are skipped
Enter commits the active option and Escape dismisses the popup without moving DOM focus
active options are scrolled into view when aria-activedescendant changes
native read-only and disabled input state, including disabled fieldset ancestry, blocks popup navigation and selection without fabricating value intent
consumer: provide a meaningful accessible input name and validation descriptions
provide concise option names, stable values, application data, and any remote-search/loading behavior
own selected-key serialization, required/validation policy, and server-side interpretation of the selected value; a named native text input submits the query, not the selected key

notes: Combobox uses the APG editable listbox-popup active-descendant model: DOM focus stays on the native text input while assistive-technology focus moves through listbox options.
Home, End, printable characters, and other native text-editing keys are not intercepted by Combobox navigation.
The active option uses aria-selected while navigating suggestions; committing with Enter updates the selected value and closes the popup.
Manual assistive-technology evidence remains owned by #1157 and is not manufactured by this mapping.

React, Vue, and Angular derive input and popup IDs from a root identity; React/Vue root id is an optional namespace, not a DOM wrapper. Input aria-controls is library-owned. Native Web and Elements retain authored markup IDs. Consumers may supply an external accessible naming relationship.

Native auto popover owns top-layer presentation and light dismissal; runtime maintains input DOM focus and clears active descendant on close. React/Vue content stays mounted while closed. The root owns independent committed selection and editable query. Controlled requests preserve owner state; accepted option commits use authored textValue (or value when textValue is absent) rather than an opaque key. Framework root query/defaultQuery is the input text contract; dynamic option relationships remain separate audit work.
